short: A revolutionary British battleship whose all-big-gun armament and steam turbine propulsion rendered all previous battleships obsolete overnight.
full:
Commissioned into the Royal Navy on 2 December 1906, HMS Dreadnought marked a profound leap in naval architecture. She was the first battleship to be armed entirely with uniform large-calibre guns, doing away with the mixed batteries of earlier designs, and the first to be powered by steam turbines, making her the fastest battleship in the world.

Her introduction was so transformative that an entire generation of subsequent battleships was simply known as 'dreadnoughts', while those preceding her were retroactively termed 'pre-dreadnoughts'. She accelerated the naval arms race between Britain and Germany, although she saw surprisingly little action during the First World War. Her only significant engagement was ramming and sinking the German submarine SM U-29 in 1915. She was paid off in 1919 and sold for scrap two years later.
